transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. I'm sure you see people with much bigger problems. But, well, mostly I just don't feel like myself anymore? 

I'm usually a pretty active guy, but lately I've just kind of stopped doing everything. I stopped hiking, and coaching... I don't even pick up my guitar anymore, or call people back. I know that's not very polite of me to ignore calls. I hope that makes sense so far? 

It's just... I'm a little embarrassed to admit this, but some days I just sit in my small rental for hours. I know there are things I need to get done, and I want to do them, but I just can't seem to make myself start. I know it probably sounds like I'm just being lazy, and I'm really sorry if it comes across that way, I promise I'm normally a very hard worker. Is... is that the kind of thing I should be telling you?
When did you first notice this change in yourself — when did you stop feeling like your usual self?

Um... well, I guess it's been a little while. I hope I'm not giving you too much unnecessary personal detail, but... I think things started kind of unraveling—though maybe 'unraveling' is too dramatic of a word, I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining. 

But it was right around the time I moved into this smaller rental, just after my divorce. That was... gosh, about a year and two months ago, I think? I tried my best to keep a positive attitude about the move and everything, I really did, but looking back, that seems to be when I just stopped bouncing back the way I usually do. Is that... does that give you the kind of timeline you need?
Over this past year, how would you describe your mood most days? Do you feel sad, empty, or down, or is it more just a lack of motivation and interest in things?

Um... well, I don't think I feel sad, exactly? I mean, I really try not to be one of those people who just sits around feeling sorry for themselves. I hope I don't come across that way, I always try to keep my chin up. 

It's really more of the second thing you mentioned... just this total lack of drive. Like I was saying earlier, about mostly just not feeling like myself anymore? It's like... I'll be sitting there in the rental, and I know I should be going for a hike, or getting ready to coach, or at least picking up my guitar like I used to. But the spark is just gone. I sit there for hours knowing there are things I need to do, and I just... I can't make myself start. I want to want to do them, I really do, but the motivation just isn't there. 

I'm so sorry if I'm just repeating what I already told you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I answering your question okay?

Besides the lack of motivation and that 'spark' being gone, have you been experiencing excessive worry or anxiety about things? Or do you notice physical tension, like muscle tightness or restlessness?

Um... no, I don't think so. I hope I'm not being unhelpful by saying no, but I really try not to let things get to me. I don't feel particularly worried or... or anxious about anything. 

And my body feels fine, really. I haven't noticed any muscle tightness or restlessness at all. Like I was saying, I mostly just sit there pretty still. I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for, or if it makes things harder for you to figure out... I just want to make sure I'm being completely honest with you. Is it okay that I don't have those kinds of symptoms?
Over this past year since the move and divorce, have you noticed any changes in your sleep — like sleeping more or less than usual? Or changes in your appetite?

Um... well, I haven't really noticed any big changes there. I hope that's alright. I mean, my sleep is pretty normal, I think. I definitely don't sleep the day away or anything like that. I always try to get up at a reasonable hour, even if I don't end up doing much. I really don't want to come across as lazy. 

And my appetite is... it's fine, really. I eat. I might not cook big meals for myself since it's just me in the rental now, but I make sure I'm eating enough. I try to take care of myself, I really do. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm not giving you very much to go on with these questions. I hope I'm not making your job too difficult by not having these issues. Am I doing okay?

When you think about activities you used to enjoy — like hiking or playing guitar — do you find that even when you do try to do them, they don't bring you pleasure or enjoyment anymore? Or is it more that you just don't feel motivated to start them in the first place?

Um... well, it's really just the motivation part, I think. I mean, I don't want you to think I've completely lost the ability to enjoy things or that I'm totally numb. I really try not to let myself get that way. 

If I actually manage to pick up the guitar, or... or if a buddy drags me out on a trail, I can still appreciate it. It's not like it feels awful or anything. It's just... getting over that initial hump of starting is so, so hard right now. Once I'm doing it, it's okay. I really hope that makes sense. I don't want to sound like I'm just making excuses for not doing things. Does that answer what you were asking?

You mentioned the divorce and move about a year ago as when things started to change. Was there any one particular event around that time — something specific that happened — that felt especially difficult or traumatic to you? Or did it feel more like a gradual wearing down after the move and divorce?

Um... I don't think there was one specific thing. I really hope I'm not being too vague, but it... it just felt more like a gradual thing. 

The divorce was tough, of course, and moving out... but I tried to handle it as best I could. I didn't want to make a big fuss or fall apart, you know? I really tried to keep it together. So, no, there wasn't any... any big, traumatic event or anything like that. Just the stress of the changes, I guess, wearing me down over time. 

I'm sorry if that's not very helpful. I know you're trying to find a starting point for all this. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. Is it okay that it was just a gradual thing and not one big event?

You mentioned your sleep and appetite are pretty normal. But I want to ask more specifically: when you do sleep, do you wake up feeling rested and energized, or do you find yourself feeling tired and sluggish even after a full night's sleep?

Um... well, I usually feel pretty okay when I wake up. I really hope that's the right answer. I mean, I wouldn't say I leap out of bed full of energy or anything, but I definitely don't feel sluggish all day. 

I try to make sure I get enough rest so I can function. I don't want to be one of those people who complains about being tired all the time, you know? I really make an effort to start my day right. So, I guess I'd say I feel adequately rested most mornings. 

I hope it's not a bad thing that I don't feel exhausted. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out. Am I answering your questions alright?

When you're sitting there in the rental for those hours, how would you describe your emotional state? Are you feeling down or low in mood during those times, or is it more neutral — like you're just... there?

Um... well, it's mostly just... neutral, I think. I really hope that makes sense. I don't want you to think I'm sitting there feeling sorry for myself or crying all day, because I'm definitely not doing that. I try really hard not to let myself get down. 

It's more like I'm just... existing, you know? Just sitting there. It's not a deep sadness or anything that I'd call depression. I really don't want to come across like I'm wallowing. It's just a quiet kind of blankness, I guess. 

I hope it's okay that I don't feel super sad during those times. I just want to be completely honest with you so you get the right idea. Does that sound like what you were asking about?

I appreciate you being so honest with me. When you think back over this past year, if you had to describe your overall emotional state — not just in those moments sitting in the rental, but throughout your days — would you say your mood has been low or sad, even if it's subtle? Or has the emotional part of your experience really just been that neutral blankness you described?

Um... I think it's mostly just been that neutral feeling. I really don't think I've been depressed or sad. I mean, I try to keep a good attitude about things, even with the divorce and everything. I don't want to be a burden on anyone or seem like I'm complaining. 

So, yeah, I'd say it's just been pretty blank. Not low or sad. I really hope that's okay to say. I know sometimes people expect you to be sad after a divorce, but I just... I haven't been. I've just been kind of flat. Is that... is that normal? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Over this entire past year since the divorce and move, has this flat mood and lack of motivation been present pretty much every day without breaks? Or have there been stretches of time — maybe weeks or months — where you felt more like your normal self before it came back?

Um... well, it's pretty much been this way the whole time. I really hope that doesn't sound like I'm just giving up or not trying to get better. I mean, things have just been kind of... unraveling, I guess, since I moved into this smaller rental after the divorce. That was about a year and two months ago. 

I haven't really had any long breaks where I felt totally normal again. I try, I really do, but it's just been a steady kind of blankness since the move. I don't want you to think I haven't been making an effort to bounce back. It's just been a continuous stretch since then. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just want to be sure I'm giving you an accurate timeline so you can help me. Is it okay that it's been going on that long without a break?

You mentioned things have been pretty steady since the move. But I want to ask more carefully: has the flatness and lack of motivation stayed at about the same level this whole year, or have there been times — even just a few weeks here or there — when you felt noticeably better, even if you didn't feel completely back to normal?

Um... I really wish I could tell you yes. I know it would probably be a much better sign if I had some weeks in there where things lifted a bit. But... honestly, no. It's pretty much just stayed at that exact same level this whole time. 

I hope you don't think I'm just letting myself go or not putting in the effort to improve. I really do try to push through it. It's just... it hasn't really changed at all. Just steady. 

I'm sorry if that's frustrating to hear, or if it makes it harder to help me. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the absolute truth so you have what you need. Is it... is it okay that it's just been the same? I'm really trying to do this right.

I want to make sure I have the timeline right. Over this entire year since the move, have there been any stretch of time — even just a few weeks or a couple of months — where the flatness lifted enough that you felt noticeably different, even if you wouldn't say you felt completely back to normal?

Oh, um... I'm so sorry, I must not have been very clear just a second ago. I definitely don't want to confuse you or mess up your notes. But... no, I really haven't noticed any weeks or months where it lifted. It's just been... steady. The whole year since I moved. 

I really wish I could give you a better answer. I know it would probably be a lot better if there were breaks in there where I felt a little more normal. I hope I'm not being difficult or making this harder for you to figure out. Does that help clear up the timeline for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.

Over this past year, have there been any times — even just a week or two — when you felt unusually energetic, more talkative than normal, or like you were taking on a lot of projects or activities with extra enthusiasm?

Um... no, I haven't really had anything like that happen. I mean, I'm sure it would be nice to have a burst of energy or enthusiasm for once, but... no. I haven't felt unusually talkative or taken on any extra projects. I mostly just try to keep my head down and get through the day. 

I really hope it's okay that my answers keep being kind of... boring, I guess? I'm not trying to be unhelpful, I promise. I just haven't had any stretches where I felt super energetic or outgoing like that. Am I giving you the right kind of information? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job answering your questions.
